_README: The game's own default tune for a known build, every slider, read off eight
screenshots on 2026-08-12. Same car and parts as
gearing-gr86-defaulttune-2026-08-12.json; this is the rest of the tabs.
It was collected as the C1 control row. It also solved Aero Balance and
killed the simplest Mechanical Balance model, neither of which anyone was
asking it to do — see aeroBalanceSolved and mechBalanceConstraint.

defaultTune._note: Every value the game shipped for this build. Units are as the screen prints them.

aeroBalanceSolved: *** WITHDRAWN THE SAME DAY. THIS SECTION IS WRONG. See
*** balance-ab-gr86-2026-08-12.json -> aeroBalanceNotSolved.
*** A second point (F 190, R 290) predicts 0.396 and measures 0.42, which
*** is five times the rounding window. There IS a bodyshell term, case A1
*** predicted it, and this section talked it away on a single point.
*** Kept unedited below because the error is the lesson: 0.4502 against a
*** printed 0.45 is NOT a four-decimal match — AB prints to two decimals,
*** so anything in [0.445,0.455] shows as 0.45. A 2-dp readout cannot
*** confirm a model to 4 dp.
AERO BALANCE IS FRONT DOWNFORCE OVER TOTAL DOWNFORCE, IN POUNDS.
Exact to every digit shown. Case A1 asked whether AB at equal sliders is
0.5 and predicted it would not be; the real answer is better, because the
slider is not a percentage at all — it is pounds of downforce, and the
balance is simply their ratio. There is no bodyshell term to discover. The
asymmetry A1 expected is just the front and rear ends having different
pound ranges.
ONE CAR, ONE POINT — the standing rule is two before a constant is general,
so this is confirmed-pending. The confirmation is free: Boston is about to
move only the rear wing for the axis test, so re-reading AB at that setting
is a second point on the same car for no extra work. A different car is the
one still owed.
WHAT IT CHANGES IN THE APP, if it holds. VMETA has aeF and aeR as
'% of range', 0-100 (index.html:559-560), and the discipline tables emit
values like aeF 60. But front and rear have DIFFERENT pound ranges — 190
and 232 sit at visibly different slider positions here — so setting both
ends to the same percentage does NOT give a predictable balance, and the
0.42-0.48 target cannot be hit through a percentage. With this solve the
app can instead say: read your two downforce numbers, and set them so
front/(front+rear) lands in the band. That is an exact instruction with an
exact target, which is what the aero section has never had.
AND IT MAKES THE REACHABILITY CHECK (A3) CHEAP. The achievable range is
[ Fmin/(Fmin+Rmax) , Fmax/(Fmax+Rmin) ]
so four readings — each wing at each end, in pounds — bracket every AB the
car can produce, and settle whether the printed target is reachable at all.
mechBalanceConstraint: MECHANICAL BALANCE IS NOT THE ANTI-ROLL BAR RATIO. That is the simplest
candidate model (M1 in MEASURE.md Phase 1) and this single row kills it:
screen prints                                            0.50
So whatever MB is, the bars alone do not set it, and the front bar being
more than twice the rear does not push the readout off centre at all.
WHAT DOES FIT, on this one row: the SPRINGS.
A pure-spring ratio lands inside the rounding of the printed value. A model
with both terms also fits provided the bar term is small. A bars-only model
cannot fit at all.
THIS IS ONE POINT AND IT CANNOT CHOOSE BETWEEN THE SURVIVORS. It is exactly
the discrimination MEASURE.md Phase 1 was designed to get, arriving free
from a screenshot taken for another purpose — but the same-ratio pair and
the spring rows are still needed, and Phase 1 now has a much better
starting hypothesis to test than it had this morning: MB is spring-led,
with the bars contributing little or nothing.
IF THAT SURVIVES, IT IS A PROBLEM FOR THE APP. The Verify In Game section
tells the user to hit Mechanical Balance 0.55-0.65 and the fine-tune advice
treats the bars as the balance lever. If MB barely responds to the bars,
that instruction is unachievable by the means the app recommends.
panelFindings: TWO THINGS ABOUT THE PERFORMANCE PANEL, both from comparing these eight
shots against the six-read repeat test taken minutes earlier on the SAME
TUNE.
1. ACCELERATION FIGURES ARE QUANTISED TO EXACTLY 1/60 SECOND. Every 0-60
and 0-100 figure recorded today is an exact multiple of 1/60:
The simulation is frame-stepped at 60 Hz and these are frame counts. So
0.0167 s is the hard resolution of the instrument, a one-frame
difference is the smallest thing it can express, and quoting three
decimals implies precision that only two of them carry.
Worth noting against the older data: the July sweep's figures (3.040,
3.056, 8.723...) are NOT multiples of 1/60. Either they came from a
different frame rate or they were not transcribed exactly. Flagged, not
resolved.
2. THE FIGURES MOVED BETWEEN THE TWO SETS, WITH THE TUNE UNCHANGED.
That is 2 frames on 0-60 and 1 on 0-100 — small, but far larger than the
repeat test's own spread, which was zero on both. Top speed held at
141.1 throughout.
THIS IS THE VARIANCE BOSTON SAID HE HAD SEEN, and it means the S0 result
is narrower than it looked: the panel is deterministic WITHIN a
continuous sitting on one screen, and not across whatever happened
between these two sets. Until we know what that was, the working rule is
that a comparison is only valid within one unbroken sitting, because a
2-frame drift will otherwise masquerade as a result.
UNRESOLVED, AND BOSTON IS THE ONLY ONE WHO KNOWS: what happened between
the repeat test and these screenshots — leaving the tuning menu, backing
out to the garage, applying the tune, a restart? The answer names the
thing that has to be held constant, and S0 should re-run across THAT
boundary rather than only across a slider nudge.
corroborations: Three of the app's numbers meet the game's default here, which is worth
recording as much as the disagreements:
- AWD centre balance 60%. The app's neutral base moved 55 -> 60 on
ForzaTune's band without ever being measured (case D3). The game's own
default for this AWD build is exactly 60.
- Tire pressure 31.0 psi. PSI.semi in index.html:523 is 31. Exact.
- Brake balance 50% and pressure 100%, which is the base the app's
And one disagreement: CASTER. The game's default here is 5.0 deg; the app
uses 6.5 for the road family (index.html:508), from ForzaTune's 5.5-6.5
band. Not necessarily wrong — a default is not an optimum — but it is the
app sitting at the top of a published band while the game ships the bottom.
notes: Front and rear aero clearly have different pound ranges: 190 and 232 sit at different slider positions on the same screen. That alone means any per-cent-of-range aero instruction is car-specific and end-specific. The default diff is strongly rear-biased on acceleration (front 30, rear 55) with very low deceleration lock at both ends (10 and 13), which is a shape worth remembering when the diff cases are designed.
